_comment: 報連相：連絡 の 講義ページ（content/articles/renraku_lecture.json）に 足した「5. 電話での 連絡」の 絵（2026-10-30 の 指定「4と5の間に『電話での連絡』を入れてください」）。参照は いまの s1（絵柄と 若手エンジニア・リーダーの 2人の アンカー）。表情は 大げさに・字と 印を 入れる（2026-10-27 の 決まり。docs/skills/codex_image_generation.md §6.7）。denwa は 1回目、リーダーが となりの 席から 電話に 出て いて 不自然だった（となりなら 話せば いい）ので、丸い 枠の 中の 別の 場所に 置いて 撮り直した。bamen は「場面で 使い分ける」の カード 4枚の 絵を 2×2 の 1枚に 描かせ、白い すきまで 切り分けた（bamen_1〜4.webp）。答え（電話・メール）の 道具は 描かない——カードの 絵は こたえを 押す 前から 見えるため。「人に よって 好きな 方法が ちがう」の 絵は 人物が ヘンディ・奥田 なので 別の 台帳（renraku_konomi.json）。
style: Warm modern anime illustration, like a friendly Japanese educational manga — clean confident black linework, flat cel shading with gentle light, bright natural daylight, soft pastel palette of sky blue, cream and coral, rounded friendly shapes. A tidy contemporary Japanese software office with real desks, chairs, windows, plants, mugs and laptops. People are drawn as real human beings with natural proportions, warm friendly faces and exactly five fingers on each hand, no tangled or merged fingers. Match the drawing style and the colours of the FIRST reference picture exactly. The junior engineer is the young man of the reference picture with short dark brown hair wearing a coral-orange shirt jacket over a white tee; the team leader is the man of the reference picture with short black hair in a navy blazer over a white shirt. This is a TEACHING picture, not a mood picture: a student who can hardly read Japanese must understand the message from the picture alone. EMOTIONS ARE BIG AND OBVIOUS, like a Japanese comedy manga — exaggerated faces and whole-body poses that read from across the room. Happy and relieved people beam with huge open smiles and sparkling eyes, raise a fist or give a thumbs-up, with little sparkles around them. Puzzled people tilt their heads under a big question mark. Manga symbols are welcome and carry the message: big question marks, exclamation marks, sweat drops, lightbulbs, sparkles, motion lines, check marks.
noText: Lettering — read this part carefully. The picture contains ONLY the words listed above, and no other writing at all. Print each Japanese word LARGE and horizontally in a bold rounded gothic Japanese font, with generous space around it — either on a soft cream label with a rounded border, or inside a white speech balloon whose tail clearly points at the person who says it. Directly above every kanji, print its reading in small hiragana (furigana), centred over that kanji, clearly separated from it, at about 45% of the kanji height, so that the kanji and the furigana both stay sharp. Words written only in hiragana or katakana take no furigana, and Latin letters and numbers take no furigana either. The readings in round brackets are for you only — never print the brackets or the reading in the brackets as text. Spell every character exactly as given. Screens, papers and whiteboards show only soft abstract shapes apart from the listed words. No other letters, numbers, logos or watermarks anywhere in the picture.
negative: Never: photo-realistic rendering, harsh shadows, extra or merged fingers, distorted hands, horror or a scary dark mood, real grief, violence, watermarks, real company logos or brand marks of any kind (no fruit logo on laptops or phones, no chat-app logos), national flags, country outlines, maps with borders, tiny cluttered text, paragraphs of text, 3D render, flat vector icon art, pictograms floating on an empty background, robots, mascots.

scenes.title: 電話は すぐに 返事が もらえる／メール・チャットは 記録が 残る
scenes.where: content/articles/renraku_lecture.json 5節「電話での 連絡」の 見出しの 下
scenes.scene: THE ONE IDEA THIS PICTURE MUST MAKE OBVIOUS: a phone call gets an answer right now, while a mail or chat message waits until the reader has time — and its words stay. One wide picture split into two equal halves by a soft vertical cream gutter, the same layout as the FIRST reference picture. At the top of each half sits one wide rounded cream label panel with two lines: a big bold first line and a smaller second line. LEFT HALF, on a pale sky-blue ground: the label panel shows a small drawn phone handset before its big first line (the first word below), and the second word below on its second line. The junior engineer sits at his desk in the lower left holding a smartphone to his ear, talking, with an eager face. The team leader is NOT in the same room: he appears in a large round manga-style phone-call inset panel in the upper right of this half, with a thick outline and a small jagged edge where it touches a curly phone-line drawn from the engineer's phone, so it is obvious the two are in different places. Inside the inset the team leader walks in a corridor of another floor, holding his phone to his ear; he has already turned on his heel to come, huge open grin, his free hand giving a big thumbs-up, motion lines around him showing how fast he answers. A white speech balloon from the team leader inside the inset says the third word below, all on ONE single line with clear room above 行 for its furigana. RIGHT HALF, on a pale mint-green ground: the label panel shows a small drawn envelope and a small drawn chat bubble before its big first line (the fourth word below), and the fifth word below on its second line. The junior engineer types calmly on his laptop with a relaxed smile; his laptop screen shows a chat window with five message bubbles stacked neatly from top to bottom as soft grey abstract bars with no readable writing, the newest bubble outlined in coral, so it is clear that every message stays on the screen. Behind him, through a glass wall, the team leader sits in a small meeting room with two colleagues; he glances down at his phone, which shows the same stacked chat bubbles, and nods with a calm smile and a small green check mark beside the phone, showing he reads it when he has time. The two halves are the same size and read left to right in one pass.
text: すぐに 返事が もらえる（すぐに へんじが もらえる）
OK！ すぐ 行くね。（OK！ すぐ いくね。）
記録が 残る（きろくが のこる）

scenes.title: 場面で 使い分ける（場面 1〜4）
scenes.where: content/articles/renraku_lecture.json 5節「場面で 使い分ける」の 伏せた カード 4枚
scenes.scene: THE ONE IDEA THIS PICTURE MUST MAKE OBVIOUS: four different work situations, each readable at a glance. One wide picture divided into FOUR EQUAL PANELS in a 2 by 2 grid, separated by clean white gutters about 24 pixels wide, with no panel touching another. Every panel is its own small scene in the bright office with the junior engineer of the reference picture. NONE of the panels shows a telephone, a smartphone, an envelope or a mail icon anywhere — the picture shows only the situation, never the tool to use. TOP-LEFT PANEL (situation 1): the junior engineer jumps up from his desk in a panic, clutching his head with both hands, huge sweat drops and wide teary eyes; on the big monitor beside him a bright red warning screen carries the word ERROR in large letters, and the server rack behind him blinks red lights with a big red cross mark; next to him the team leader's chair is EMPTY, with the leader's navy blazer hanging on its back, and the junior looks at the empty chair desperately — the leader is not here and is needed right now. TOP-RIGHT PANEL (situation 2): the junior engineer stands at a large wall schedule board and slides one coloured meeting card from a higher row down to the next row, a thick soft coral arrow showing the move, with two large clock faces beside it, the first showing two o'clock and the second showing three o'clock; behind him six teammates work at their desks across the room, so it is clear that the whole team must know about the change. BOTTOM-LEFT PANEL (situation 3): the junior engineer sits at his desk holding up one printed estimate sheet that shows a big gold coin drawing and soft grey bars, next to a desk calendar page with one day circled in red; in a round inset in the corner, a client — a middle-aged man in a grey business suit in a different company's office with its own lobby — waits politely, showing this is a person outside the company. BOTTOM-RIGHT PANEL (situation 4): the junior engineer types on his laptop with a frustrated face, wavy worried mouth and sweat drops; his laptop screen shows three long chat messages stacked one under another as soft grey bars; in a round inset in the corner the team leader reads the same messages on his laptop with swirling confused eyes under a big question mark, showing the messages are not getting through. The four panels are the same size and read left to right, top to bottom.
